title: NexaComms \u000B Procurement: MSA/DPA, SLAs, Pricing & Onboarding
summary: High-level procurement call to review Redwood MSA and DPA terms, confirm SLAs and uptime targets, discuss pricing approval path, and agree onboarding pilot. Redwood to send redlined MSA, SOC2 and DPA, and a pilot quote. Customer requested tighter data residency language, KMS/HSM details, and a legal follow-up next week.
topics: Vendor onboarding and pilot (Dedicated vs Private)
next_steps: Jordan to send redlined MSA and DPA template by 2026-11-12
Priya to share SOC2 Type II and security whitepaper link
Jordan to provide pilot pricing and dedicated capacity quote by 2026-11-10
Schedule legal follow-up with Leah for 2026-11-15
Set technical deep-dive for Samir and Rina with Priya (week of 2026-11-15)
action_items: Jordan Reyes: Send redlined MSA and DPA by 2026-11-12
Priya Malhotra: Share SOC2 report, network diagram, and KMS integration notes by 2026-11-09
Mark Chen: Confirm internal pricing approval timeline and PO owner by 2026-11-13
Leah Ortiz: Prepare redlines and identify any non-starter clauses by 2026-11-15
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for joining, i see Mark, Leah, Samir and Rina, appreciate you taking the time. we'll run about 45 to 60 minutes, want to make sure we lock next steps for legal and the pilot.
[00:18] Mark (NexaComms): yep thanks Jordan, on our side im mark, head of procurement, Leah's our counsel, Samir is CTO and Rina heads security. main goal today is to get alignment on MSA/DPA language and any SLA must-haves so we can route to finance.
[00:33] Leah (NexaComms Legal): quick note, we have a 3 week procurement window if possible; we need to know what are the non-negotiable clauses for Redwood.
[00:42] Jordan: understood, we can flag items but typically our MSA is fairly standard. Priya from our solutions team will join for technical and security Qs.
[00:50] Priya (Redwood SE): hi all, thanks. technical items i expect: vpc/private deployment options, kms/hsm integration, retention, and SLAs around latency/availability.
[01:05] Samir (CTO): on latency, we have strict p95 requirements under 500ms for the real-time product, can you confirm that on hosted you can meet that or we should consider dedicated?
[01:18] Priya: so hosted can be very fast for many workloads but for strict p95 under 500ms we usually recommend Redwood Dedicated or private deployment pinned to reserved gpus. there is also batching and kv cache behavior that changes tail latency, so we should profile with your payload.
[01:40] Rina (Security): regarding data residency, we need all logs and user content to stay in eu-west-1, and full audit logs. also we require BYOK support and KMS/HSM details.
[01:54] Jordan: we support region pinning and have customer-managed KMS options for Private. for Hosted we can offer region-specific tenancy but the KMS integration differs, i'll get you the exact flow.
[02:10] Leah: on the DPA side, retention and deletion obligations need to be explicit. our legal is pushing for 30 day deletion of user content unless archived for compliance. is that feasible?
[02:22] Priya: we can offer configurable retention, but for some features like kv caching there are short-lived caches that are ephemeral. we can add explicit terms in DPA to cover those semantics.
[02:36] Mark: pricing \u2014 finance wants to know if pilot pricing converts to committed rates and what the approval path is for purchase orders.
[02:45] Jordan: pilot pricing is usually time-boxed and will be a separate quote. if you move to Dedicated we can convert pilot usage to committed capacity with a pro-rated credit. i'll include that in the quote.
[02:58] Samir: security \u2014 SOC2, iso, pen tests?
[03:02] Priya: we have SOC2 Type II and pen test summaries, i'll share redacted reports. also note we support SSO/SAML and role-based access via RBAC in the console.
[03:18] Rina: ok we'll need the SOC2 cert and network architecture diagram. also any third-party subprocessors list.
[03:28] Jordan: copy that, priya will send SOC2, whitepaper, and the subprocessor list.
[03:34] [05:10] Leah: on indemnities and liability caps, our legal usually pushes for mutual cap at 2x fees; can we discuss where Redwood stands?
[05:22] Jordan: our standard liability cap is 1x fees, with exceptions we can discuss for enterprise deals. i'll note this as an item for redlines.
[05:34] Leah: and data breach notification terms \u2014 72 hours?
[05:37] Priya: 72 hours is our standard SLA for notification, yes.
[05:42] Mark: service credits \u2014 how are slas measured and credited?
[05:46] Jordan: uptime is measured per calendar month per route/model; for Dedicated we can commit to 99.9 uptime with credits, Hosted is 99.5 standard, details in SLA. if you need higher we can discuss a custom SLA in the contract.
[06:03] Samir: curious about fallback \u2014 if Dedicated capacity is saturated what happens to production calls?
[06:09] Priya: we have smart routing and fallback policies \u2014 you can choose to failover to a compatible model variant or to a hosted pool; we can set throttling and hard limits. we'll demo the routing policies in the tech deep-dive.
[06:28] Mark: timeline \u2014 finance needs a PO issued by 2026-11-24 to hit this quarter. is that realistic?
[06:35] Jordan: yes if legal finishes redlines quickly. our aim is to have redlined MSA to you within 4 business days.
[06:45] Leah: ok hard stop for us is no surprise data export rights and clear deletion obligations.
[06:52] Jordan: noted.
[09:00] Priya: quick technical note \u2014 KV cache and prefix caching can reduce cost but we should align on what is stored and retention. also quantization choices impact inference speed and cost.
[09:15] Samir: are there on-prem options? we are evaluating Private deploy for regulated workloads.
[09:20] Priya: yes, Redwood Private offers VPC/on-prem packages with customer-managed control plane. it supports KMS/HSM, offline deploys, and you can request air-gapped setups, though that adds lead time and operational support.
[09:36] Rina: can you commit to no subprocessing in certain geos or white-listed subprocessors only?
[09:42] Jordan: we can include subprocessors list and in DPA indicate restricted subprocessors by region, we'll need legal to sign off on the list.
[09:50] [12:00] Mark: i also want to surface procurement's concern about pricing elasticity; if usage spikes will we get charged unpredictably?
[12:07] Jordan: for Dedicated you get predictable per-minute or per-GPU committed rates; Hosted is usage-based so spikes can affect costs. we also offer burst policies and budget caps to prevent runaway charges.
[12:20] Leah: regarding audits, do you provide audit logs for token-level activity? we need forensic capability.
[12:27] Priya: yes console provides token-level cost and latency breakdowns and audit logs; retention windows and export formats will be in the security docs.
[12:40] Mark: ok good.
[15:00] Jordan: next steps recap \u2014 we'll send the MSA, DPA, SOC2, and pilot quote. any blockers on our side?
[15:12] Leah: i need to evaluate the indemnity and liability cap, if 1x fee stands we may push for carveouts.
[15:20] Jordan: understood, please flag those clauses.
[15:25] Samir: technical deep-dive \u2014 we want a test harness to run p95 latency tests and a sample dataset. can Redwood run performance benchmarks or do we run them?
[15:36] Priya: we can run benchmarks with a joint test, we'll need 1-2 representative payloads and expected concurrency. i'll coordinate.
[15:46] Rina: security will also want a threat model review; will priya lead?
[15:51] Priya: yes i'll lead that and bring our security folks if needed.
[18:00] Mark: one admin Q \u2014 onboarding: how long to go live for a small pilot of 2 models with around 50k tokens/day?
[18:08] Jordan: for Hosted pilot you can be live in days; Dedicated pilot might take 2-4 weeks to provision. private on-prem takes longer.
[18:20] Leah: please include a statement about data segregation in the MSA for pilot data.
[18:26] Jordan: will do.
[22:00] Priya: i'll post links in the follow-up \u2014 SOC2 whitepaper, security architecture diagram, subprocessors list, pilot quote spreadsheet (link: https://redwood.example.com/quote/CRM-32819), and standard MSA/DPA pdf.
[22:18] Samir: the quote link returns 403 for me earlier, maybe an internal link issue.
[22:24] Jordan: noted i'll ensure access and resend with perms.
[30:00] Leah: a couple wording asks \u2014 can we get a clause that requires data deletion certification within 30 days after termination?
[30:09] Jordan: we can provide certification language, our legal prefers 60 days in some cases but we'll propose 30 days for pilot/customers.
[30:20] Mark: finance needs a line item for SLA credits and the formula in the quote.
[30:27] Jordan: we'll include the SLA credit table.
[36:00] Priya: technical note \u2014 if you need p95 under 500ms we should plan to run both Hosted and Dedicated benchmarks, i suspect Dedicated will be required for strict real-time routing.
[36:10] Samir: ok plan on that.
[40:00] Jordan: recap again \u2014 actions are Jira-style: redwood sends redline and docs; customer sends legal redlines; schedule legal sync for 11-15 and technical deep-dive week of 11-15.
[40:18] Leah: yes, i'll book the legal sync pending internal calendar.
[41:00] Mark: any final questions?
[41:05] Jordan: none from us, thanks everyone.
[41:08] Priya: thanks we'll follow up with links and the pilot quote by Tuesday.
[41:15] Samir: thanks all.
[41:20] Rina: thanks.
[52:00] Meeting ended.
